rows.subtype: Approach: setting a goal with an amount and date [Thinking]
rows.description: A teen wants a secondhand bicycle costing 4,000 rupees in six months, divides it into a weekly saving figure, and finds it is more realistic than he thought.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, values-first planning

rows.description: On the day the allowance arrives, a student moves a fixed portion into a separate envelope or savings account before spending anything, so saving does not depend on leftover money.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: tracking spending and finding leaks [Action]
rows.description: A teen writes down every purchase for a month, discovers that snacks and mobile top-ups take a third of her money, and trims those two areas by choice.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: earning extra through small honest work [Action]
rows.description: A student offers to tutor younger neighbours for a small fee after checking with parents, and directs part of the earnings to the same goal, which speeds it up.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: spending impulsively at the first temptation [Pitfall]
rows.description: A teen with saved money sees a sale online and buys a pair of shoes on impulse, then finds that the bicycle goal is set back by two months.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: values-first planning

rows.description: A student buys expensive treats to match classmates at the canteen, feeling left out otherwise, and finds at month end that little remains for what he actually wanted.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: making saving visible with a chart [Action]
rows.description: A teen draws a savings thermometer on her wall and colours it in each week, and seeing it fill keeps the effort going through weeks when spending feels more fun.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: falling for easy-money schemes online [Pitfall]
rows.description: A teen sees an online promise to double savings in a week through a game app, imagines quick success, and nearly sends money before a parent explains that such offers are usually frauds.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: adjusting the goal after a shortfall [Revision]
rows.description: After a month with unexpected school expenses, a student extends the target date by four weeks and lowers the weekly amount rather than abandoning the plan altogether.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: splitting money into save, spend and give [Thinking]
rows.description: A teen decides that half goes to the goal, a third to spending and the rest to family gifts or charity, which balances her wants and values so the plan feels fair.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action
